support_cases.note: Support cases summarized with question/answer summaries, answer_confidence, topic, product_area, priority, and closure_reason.

metadata.documentation_repo: domo-documentation-hub (Mintlify): ~1,813 KB articles in s/article/, 115 topics in s/topic/, 473 portal pages
metadata.what_this_is: Topics discussed in the Domo community forums AND/OR surfaced by Domo support cases that are MISSING or only PARTIALLY covered in the documentation. Each gap carries forum signal and/or support-case signal; support-derived gaps were mined from cases closed as resolvable by docs (training / Lite Education / KB referral) and verified against the repo.
metadata.method: Forum threads were clustered into topics by category, each cluster's specific question was checked against the actual repo (title + content grep, then reading candidate articles), and only 'none' (undocumented) and 'partial' (related article misses the specific gap) topics were kept. 'covered' topics and out-of-scope/negligible items were dropped.

scoring.impact_estimate: area_weight * gap_severity(none=1.0, partial=0.6) * feature_request_modifier(true=0.6, false=1.0) + 0.12 boost for security/PDP/data-correctness/deprecation/regression signals
scoring.recency_factor: by latest post year (2026=1.0 down to 2019=0.2)
scoring.note: is_feature_request topics are de-prioritized (they are mostly product gaps, not doc gaps) but retained because their current behavior/limitations and community workarounds are still documentable.
scoring.combined: combined_score = forum_score*(1 + 0.15*support_strength) for forum gaps; for support-only gaps, combined_score = 100*(0.55*support_strength + 0.45*impact), impact = area_weight * severity(none=1.0,partial=0.6) * discovery_confidence. support_strength = 0.50*log-scaled num_cases(cap 60) + 0.30*low_confidence_ratio + 0.20*documentable_resolution_ratio. Final list is re-ranked by combined_score. forum_rank/forum_score preserve the original forum-only ranking.

field_notes.recommendation: 'new' = create a new article; 'update' = extend an existing article
field_notes.suggested_location: for 'new': where the article should live + nav group; for 'update': which existing article(s) to extend and what to add
field_notes.documentation_status: 'none' = nothing in the repo addresses it; 'partial' = a related article exists but misses the specific gap
field_notes.combined_score: drives rank & priority. forum_score/forum_rank/forum_priority preserve the original forum-only values.
field_notes.priority: banded from combined_score with the forum thresholds (Critical>=75, High>=60, Medium>=45, else Low). Support corroboration can only raise a forum gap's priority, never lower it.
field_notes.support_signal: forum gaps: high-confidence matched support cases (num_cases) + loose_related_cases, confidence/closure/priority breakdowns, representative_cases. support-derived gaps: cluster size, example_cases, representative_questions, discovery_confidence.

metadata.updated: 2026-06-05: cross-referenced against Domo support cases; added support-derived net-new gaps
metadata.support_signal_method: Each forum gap was matched to support cases via TF-IDF cosine over case question_summary/topic/product_area with a rare-anchor-term gate (lexical, approximate). support_signal.num_cases counts HIGH-CONFIDENCE matches (cosine>=0.20); loose_related_cases counts weaker keyword matches (0.12-0.20). Net-new support gaps were extracted from documentable-resolution cases not tied to any forum gap, then repo-verified.

gaps.topic: Window functions in Beast Mode (RANK, LAG, running/cumulative totals) and using them as filters / Top N
gaps.description: Very large recurring cluster on SQL window functions in Beast Mode: RANK/DENSE_RANK (with or without a date column), LAG for MoM/WoW change, SUM(SUM(x)) OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) for running/cumulative totals, 'latest value' logic, Top N (+ 'Others' bucketing), dynamic row numbering, and the recurring limitation that a window-function Beast Mode cannot be used as a card/dashboard filter. Community experts repeatedly supply the same handful of patterns.
gaps.gap_detail: Need a consolidated, example-driven Beast Mode window-functions reference: RANK/DENSE_RANK ordering by any column, LAG for period-over-period change, SUM(SUM(x)) OVER running totals, 'latest value', Top N + Others via RANK() OVER, dynamic row numbering, plus the documented limitation that window-function Beast Modes can't be card filters (workarounds: Limit Rows + sort, compute RANK in Magic ETL) and that window functions aren't autocompleted in the editor / aren't in the Functions Reference.
gaps.suggested_location: New KB article in s/article/, e.g. 'Sample Beast Mode Calculations: Window Functions' (RANK/DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD, running totals via SUM(SUM(x)) OVER, Top N + Others, row numbering), linked from the Beast Mode Functions Reference Guide sample-transforms list and the Beast Mode topic page (s/topic/0TO5w000000ZanAGAS/beast-mode.mdx). Add a window-functions section to the Functions Reference Guide. Document the 'can't filter a card by a window-function Beast Mode' limitation in Troubleshooting Beast Mode Calculations and the FAQ.

gaps.topic: Preview-vs-run discrepancies, 'Not Runnable', and silent multi-output non-update in Magic ETL
gaps.description: ETLs preview perfectly on sampled rows but fail or produce wrong/blank results on full run, including a vague 'Not Runnable' error, JSON-split differences at full volume, timezone-affected date filters, and a dataset not updating despite a 'Successful' run. Separately, multi-output dataflows are marked 'Successful' as soon as the first output indexes, so cards on slower outputs render blank.
gaps.gap_detail: Document why preview (sampled, ~400k/10k rows) can pass while a full run fails or differs (NULL/dirty values, JSON/string splits, timezone/preview limits), how to diagnose 'Not Runnable', and that 'Successful' status does not guarantee all outputs are indexed (downstream cards refresh against not-yet-ready data).
gaps.suggested_location: Add a troubleshooting section to s/article/360043427953.mdx (DataFlow Troubleshooting and FAQs): why preview can pass while a full run fails/differs (sampling, nulls, JSON splits, timezone), how to read 'Not Runnable', and that a 'Successful' multi-output run may not have indexed all outputs yet.

gaps.topic: DataFlow ownership cannot be a group; outputs are owned by the DataFlow owner
gaps.description: Users repeatedly ask to assign a DataFlow (and its output DataSets) to a group, to give a DataFlow multiple owners, or are confused that a new output they created is owned by the DataFlow owner rather than themselves.
gaps.gap_detail: Cases surface several confirmed product limitations/behaviors that aren't clearly documented: (1) a DataFlow can have only one owner and cannot be owned by a group, (2) output DataSets created by a DataFlow are owned by the DataFlow owner (not whoever added the output), so the owner must share them, and (3) sharing an ETL means sharing the output DataSet, not transferring edit rights. gaps.topic: User identity reconciliation under SSO: duplicate accounts, employee-ID-as-email, name overwrites, and email changes
gaps.description: After enabling or migrating SSO, customers see identity mismatches: existing Domo accounts get duplicated because the IdP returns an employee ID instead of email; display names are overwritten by email addresses; and email-address changes for SSO users don't take effect through the normal flow (must use bulk import). Because email is Domo's unique user key, IdP misconfiguration silently creates new users.
